client: It's hard to widen that narrative when it's just me tackling everything in my role. I tried explaining this to my line manager, but she doesn't fully grasp my workload.

answer_final: Your manager sounds unsympathetic. That's very frustrating. A lot of people are in your situation in this pandemic: too much work, not enough help.. Do you want to leave the company? Look for greener pastures?
client: I understand the importance of communication. I've tried discussing the issue, but they're hesitant to hire more staff. My only option is to convey my concerns through my line manager to higher management.

user: At the moment I'm not getting outside as much as I should, I do enjoy gaming but it's hard to find time. I've been working 14 hour days all week! My boyfriend tries to tell me to switch off but it's hard when I know there's all this work waiting to be done.
answer_final: You could try setting aside an evening or two a week for time with your BF. Just walk out of the office. Try to set some boundaries.. That might seem dangerous and risky, but sometimes it's important to set boundaries.. If you don't do that, then the managers can just keep taking advantage of you and your work ethic.
client: Taking mindful pauses sounds promising, but with 14-hour workdays, it's tough. My boyfriend encourages breaks, and I enjoy gaming, though balancing all this feels challenging lately.

user: Yeah, he says the same kind of thing, that I need to be firmer and just leave when I'm due to. I guess the only way for them to truely see is for the work to just not get done as there's no time!

client: My boyfriend suggests the same, taking firmer stands on work hours. I'm realizing gaming can be a peaceful escape. Maybe it's time to let some tasks go unfinished.

user: I guess I do feel powerless, I feel like they never really listen to what I'm saying, they just act as if they are but then ignore me.

However, if you leave work early (after 9 hours, say), then they might notice you. Are you willing to take a risk?

Consider externalizing these work challenges, naming them separately from yourself, and finding empowerment in setting boundaries to preserve peace through gaming.
